---
title: "PDF, Typst and EPUB"
custom-callout:
  todo:
    title: "To do"
    icon-symbol: "fa-pen-to-square"
    color: "pink"
  thumbs-up:
    title: "Great job!"
    icon-symbol: "fa-thumbs-up"
    color: "#008000"
  test:
    title: "Test feature"
    color: "#801410"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
  pdf: default
  typst:
    output-file: qcustom-callout-formats-typst.pdf
  epub:
    custom-callout:
      todo:
        icon-symbol: "📝"
      thumbs-up:
        icon-symbol: "👍"
filters:
  - custom-callout
---

Custom callouts keep their colors and icons in PDF, Typst and EPUB output, not just in HTML and RevealJS.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html:js"}
This page is also rendered to each of those formats: use the links under **Other Formats** to download it as a PDF, a Typst PDF or an EPUB, and compare its callouts with the ones below.
:::

## A heading as the title

A heading at the top of a callout becomes its title in every format.

## What each format supports

| Format | `color` | FontAwesome icons | Emoji and other symbols |
|--------|---------|-------------------|-------------------------|
| HTML and RevealJS | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| PDF | Yes | Yes, from Font Awesome 5 | Plain ASCII text only |
| Typst | Yes | Yes, from Font Awesome 6 | Yes, when a font has them |
| EPUB | Yes | No | Yes |

- **Colors.** Hex colors, CSS color names such as `"pink"`, and `rgb()` colors work in every format. Other CSS colors, such as `hsl()`, work in HTML and RevealJS. Elsewhere the callout keeps Quarto's default color, and the render log has a warning.
- **Icons that can't be shown.** When a format can't show an icon, a colored callout shows the warning triangle instead, and the render log has a warning.
- **PDF** uses the `fontawesome5` LaTeX package, which has the Font Awesome 5 icons. An icon is found under any of its names, so `fa-house` shows Font Awesome 5's `home` icon. An icon added after Font Awesome 5 shows the warning triangle.
- **EPUB** can't show FontAwesome icons, because they need the Font Awesome fonts, which an extension can't add to an EPUB.
- **GitHub Markdown** (`format: gfm`) has only five alert types, so a custom callout becomes a `> [!NOTE]` alert with the callout's title.
- **Word** output shows custom callouts with Quarto's default styling.

## Different icons for each format

Settings under a format replace the ones at the top level for that format only. This page uses Font Awesome icons, which EPUB can't show, so its EPUB version uses emoji instead:

```yaml
---
title: "PDF, Typst and EPUB"
custom-callout:
  todo:
    title: "To do"
    icon-symbol: "fa-pen-to-square"
    color: "pink"
  thumbs-up:
    title: "Great job!"
    icon-symbol: "fa-thumbs-up"
    color: "#008000"
  test:
    title: "Test feature"
    color: "#801410"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
  pdf: default
  typst:
    output-file: qcustom-callout-formats-typst.pdf
  epub:
    custom-callout:
      todo:
        icon-symbol: "📝"
      thumbs-up:
        icon-symbol: "👍"
filters:
  - custom-callout
---
```
